source: CLAUDE.md rule 10 footnote; sim-exp-bridge validate.py; agentic-microscope plan-check

lessons.claim: The unwired checker -- a check that exists, is documented, passes, and is not connected to the thing it describes. CLAUDE.md rule 10's footnote records three in this repository (bd-intake section 2.1's empty-goal blocker: written twice, enforced zero times, walked past by 2 of 8 cases which then produced 85 runs; A4's grep: 7 false hits, never a real check; health.gate(): reachable only from a sibling tool, so no run ever gated itself). Two more turned up in 2026-09-16 in two other repositories built independently by the same person: the bridge's quantity.chain, documented as 'Required for the cycle check (rule R5)' with zero occurrences in the validator and zero in any fixture; and agentic-microscope's plan-check, under which three of a plan's citations pointed at entries existing only on another branch -- the ROI, the exposure and the 520 fps, i.e. the entire envelope eight rounds of work had been reasoning against -- while every check passed because nothing read a link. Five instances, three repositories, so it is a property of the practice and not of one codebase. DISTINCT from the estimate-instead-of-measure pattern: that one targets numbers, this one targets the checks, and passing a check is what makes it invisible. The only defence found so far is watching a rule fire: a negative fixture per rule, and inline branch checks for rules with more than one path (the bridge's R6 has five).
